newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsair to up ex-Paris cargo rates to Fr.W.Indies.
newsitem.headline: Corsair to up ex-Paris cargo rates to Fr.W.Indies.

text.p: Aero Cargo International, cargo agent for French airline Corsair, said it planned to increase ex-Paris cargo rates to the French West Indies, effective November 1.

Corsair, which is owned by French tour operator, Nouvelles Frontieres, currently operates a daily Boeing 747 passenger service from Paris to the region - Pointe a Pitre (Guadeloupe) and Fort de France (Martinique).

"The increases work out at about five percent and are in anticipation of reduced capacity on the route with Air Liberte likely to withdraw its services at the end of the month," an Aero Cargo official told Reuters.
Air Liberte, which was put under legal administration last week, operates a daily McDonnell Douglas DC10-30 passenger service to the French West Indies.
"Air Liberte has been offering discounts of around 30 percent on average cargo rates," the official added.
Air Outre Mer (AOM), which operates a daily DC10 passenger service between Paris and the French West Indies had decided on similar rates increases to the Caribbean, the official said.
However, when contacted, AOM said it could not comment on the likelihood of rates increases.
No one was available for comment at Air France, the other main carrier on the route. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
